references.text: The implementation of Jethro's advice: the leaders judged the people at all times, and they brought the difficult cases to Moses.
Moses recounts how judges were to hear both small and large cases, and bring the difficult cases to him.
The command to appoint judges and officials who shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
God commands Moses to gather seventy elders who shall bear the burden of the people together with him, so that he does not bear it alone.
Jehoshaphat appointed judges in the land to judge the people, with instructions to bring difficult cases to Jerusalem.
The apostles delegate practical tasks to others so they can devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word, a similar principle of sharing responsibility.
Numbers 11:17 shows the spiritual dimension of 'bearing the burden together,' which was first proposed as an administrative solution in Exodus 18.
Leviticus 19:15 gives the ethical norm for justice that the delegated judges in Exodus 18 are to follow.
Solomon's prayer in 1 Kings 3:9 reflects Moses' challenge with the great people, but is resolved through wisdom rather than delegation.
